stories.title: Vitalik Buterin lays out Ethereum's path to 2030
stories.summary: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin outlined a long-term vision for the network through 2030. He described Ethereum as more than a simple blockchain. The Block and CoinDesk both covered the vision the same day.
stories.whyItMatters: Buterin's roadmap shapes developer priorities. It also shapes investor expectations for Ethereum's long-term direction.
whatToWatch: Details of the 2030 roadmap as they emerge
Developer and community reaction
questions: What concrete technical changes support the 'beyond blockchain' claim?

sources.title: ‘It’s really not just a blockchain anymore’: Vitalik Buterin maps Ethereum’s path to 2030
Vitalik Buterin maps Ethereum’s shift beyond a blockchain in sweeping 2030 vision

stories.title: SEC staff's staking-token split highlights exit risks in staked ETH tokens
stories.summary: SEC staff drew a distinction between different staking-token structures. CryptoSlate reports the split highlights exit risks in staked ETH tokens. The report does not say which products face the most risk.
stories.whyItMatters: The distinction could change how regulators treat liquid-staking products. That matters for anyone who holds or issues staked ETH tokens.
whatToWatch: Whether the SEC issues formal guidance beyond staff comments
Reaction from staked-ETH token issuers
questions: Which staked ETH products face the most exit risk under this split?

sources.title: SEC staff’s staking-token split spotlights the exit risks behind staked ETH tokens

stories.title: Cosmos network intercepts 1.23 million stolen ATOM
stories.summary: The Cosmos network intercepted 1.23 million stolen ATOM tokens. CryptoSlate reports that a community governance vote must approve any refund. The vote has not yet happened.
stories.whyItMatters: The case shows that governance, not just code, decides whether stolen crypto gets returned. That matters for readers who track how blockchains recover stolen funds.
whatToWatch: The outcome of the governance vote
A timeline for the refund process

sources.title: Cosmos intercepts 1.23 million stolen ATOM but refunds now wait on governance vote

stories.title: Researchers weigh three fixes for Bitcoin's quantum-computing risk
stories.summary: Decrypt reports that researchers are testing three approaches to Bitcoin's quantum-computing risk. Future quantum computers could break the cryptography that secures Bitcoin wallets. The report gives no timeline for any fix.
stories.whyItMatters: Quantum computing could someday threaten the cryptography that secures Bitcoin. Early work on fixes matters for long-term holders.
whatToWatch: Which approach gains support from developers
Any proposed timeline for a fix
questions: How soon could quantum computers threaten Bitcoin's cryptography?
What trade-offs come with each fix?

sources.title: Bitcoin's Quantum Problem: Three Ways Researchers Are Trying to Fix It

stories.title: SEC staff: token buybacks alone don't make crypto a security
stories.summary: SEC staff said a project's token buyback does not by itself make the token a security. Decrypt reports the network must also work as intended for that view to apply. The comments are informal staff guidance, not a formal rule.
stories.whyItMatters: The guidance gives projects more clarity on how to structure buybacks. That reduces one source of regulatory uncertainty for token issuers.
whatToWatch: Whether projects change buyback programs in response
Any formal rulemaking that follows
questions: What counts as a network that 'works' under this test?
Is this staff view binding on the SEC?

sources.title: SEC Staff Says Token Buybacks Don't Make Crypto a Security—If the Network Works

stories.title: Collateral schemes could make Ethereum feel instant
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that collateral-based mechanisms could make Ethereum transactions feel instant to users. Actual settlement on Ethereum still takes time. The approach works around speed, rather than changing it.
stories.whyItMatters: Perceived speed affects Ethereum's standing against faster blockchains. That matters for payments and trading use cases.
whatToWatch: Which projects adopt these collateral mechanisms
Whether demand for faster base-layer settlement eases
questions: Who bears the loss if a transaction later fails to settle?

sources.title: Ethereum is not instant, but collateral could make it feel that way

stories.title: Bitget freezes XRP withdrawals after 27 million stolen tokens move
stories.summary: Exchange Bitget froze XRP withdrawals after 27 million stolen XRP tokens moved. CryptoSlate reports the freeze but gives few details on the original theft.
stories.whyItMatters: Exchange freezes after stolen funds move show how exchanges respond to theft in real time. That matters for tracking crypto security incidents.
whatToWatch: Whether Bitget lifts the freeze
Any identification of the parties behind the stolen tokens
questions: Where and when were the 27 million XRP stolen?
Will any of the funds be recovered?

sources.title: Bitget freezes XRP withdrawals as 27M stolen tokens move

stories.title: New Bitcoin proposal would rescue locked multisig wallets, at a cost
stories.summary: A new proposal aims to rescue Bitcoin multisig wallets that are locked. CryptoSlate reports the fix carries a hidden trade-off. The report does not detail the cost.
stories.whyItMatters: Any change to Bitcoin's wallet rules draws scrutiny. It can affect the security assumptions that existing holders rely on.
whatToWatch: What the hidden trade-off turns out to be
Developer response to the proposal
questions: What is the hidden cost of this proposal?
Which locked wallets would it help?

sources.title: New Bitcoin proposal rescues locked multisig wallets – At a hidden cost

stories.title: Riot Platforms repays $200 million credit facility
stories.summary: Bitcoin miner Riot Platforms repaid a $200 million credit facility. Cointelegraph reports the company also released the collateral that backed the loan.
stories.whyItMatters: Paying down debt strengthens a major public miner's balance sheet. That is a signal for the financial health of the mining sector.
whatToWatch: How Riot uses the freed-up collateral
Riot's next earnings report for balance-sheet detail
questions: What was the collateral, and how will Riot use it now?

sources.title: Riot Platforms repays $200M credit facility, releases collateral

stories.title: Tokenized stocks could stop trading for up to three months
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that tokenized stock products could face trading halts of up to three months. The report frames this as a risk that investors may not expect. It does not name the exact trigger.
stories.whyItMatters: Tokenized stocks are marketed partly on easy access and liquidity. A months-long freeze risk undercuts that pitch.
whatToWatch: Which platforms carry this risk
Any response from issuers or regulators

sources.title: Why your tokenized stock could stop trading for three months

stories.title: Visa lowers its reported stablecoin volume figures
stories.summary: Visa cut the stablecoin transaction volume it reports. CryptoSlate notes there is no clear evidence that actual stablecoin payment activity fell. The gap raises questions about how Visa compiles the figures.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoin volume numbers are often cited as proof of real payment adoption. A downward revision affects how much to trust that narrative.
whatToWatch: Whether Visa explains the change in method
Other data providers' stablecoin volume figures, for comparison
questions: Why did Visa cut the reported figures?
Does other data support or contradict the revision?

sources.title: Visa cuts reported stablecoin volume but there’s no proof payments fell

stories.title: Quebec regulator warns Pump.fun lacks authorization for some Canadian investors
stories.summary: Quebec's financial regulator, the AMF, warned that Pump.fun is not authorized to solicit certain Canadian investors. CryptoSlate reports the warning but gives no further detail.
stories.whyItMatters: The warning shows regulators are tightening enforcement of solicitation rules against popular crypto platforms.
whatToWatch: Whether other Canadian regulators issue similar warnings
Pump.fun's response to the AMF
questions: Will Pump.fun seek proper authorization in Quebec?

sources.title: Pump Fun is not authorized to solicit some Canadian investors, AMF warns
